title: Customize themes and prompts
description: Choose a color theme and shell prompt, see what controls the effective profile, and apply the choice to supported tools.

sections.title: Choose the right setting
paragraphs: A theme provides colors for supported tools. A prompt profile chooses the shell prompt, such as the full Starship configuration or the native classic prompt. A preset saves a theme and prompt pair together.
Use list before setting an ID. Available themes come from the installed colorscheme module, and available prompts and presets come from their manifests. The current selection is marked in the list.
sections.code:
smu theme list
smu prompt list
smu preset list
smu profile

sections.title: Save your choices
paragraphs: This example saves Nord and the classic shell prompt. Run the corresponding list commands first to confirm both IDs are present on your machine. The choices are saved in ~/.config/set-me-up/profile.env.
Open a new terminal to check shell startup behavior. If an existing terminal still uses an old prompt, check the effective choice there and again in a new shell.
sections.code:
smu theme set nord
smu prompt set classic
smu profile

sections.title: Apply the theme to supported tools
paragraphs: If you also want to update the tool adapters provided by the colorschemes module, apply the current theme. Review the active theme before running this command because it updates files for supported tools. You can also apply a theme as part of saving it with smu theme set <theme> --apply.
Use a preset when you want a known theme and prompt combination. Setting a preset saves both choices. Add --apply when you also intend to provision the colorschemes module.

sections.title: Find which value wins
paragraphs: For each choice, the environment variable takes precedence, followed by its machine-local TOML file, the saved profile, and the default. If smu says it saved a new value but the old value still appears, start by checking the environment in that terminal.

sections.title: Check the profile after changing it
paragraphs: The theme doctor checks the selected theme’s support files. The prompt doctor checks whether the selected prompt has what it needs. Use the profile doctor to check resolved configuration and identify stale or missing generated state.
When a generated target contains a different local configuration, preserve your file and review the conflict before asking the adapter to rewrite it.
sections.code:
smu theme doctor nord
smu prompt doctor classic
smu profile doctor
